components.name: CharacterConsistencyValidator.checkPronounAgreement / findIncorrectPronouns (pronoun_gender_mismatch, severity major)
components.lines: class 73; validate 84-147; checkPronounAgreement 274-310; findIncorrectPronouns 312-409; gender manifest 149-243 (RC2.2 genderOverride ctor 82)
components.what: Pattern classes: wrong SUBJECT (he/she, lines 391-394), wrong OBJECT (him/her, 397-400), wrong POSSESSIVE only 'his' for female chars (403) — 'her'-as-possessive for male chars rides the object check at 400. NO reflexive (himself/herself) and NO 'hers' checks anywhere (391-405). Does NOT strip dialogue — quoted speech is scanned as narration. Antecedent association is pure name-in-sentence: only sentences that literally contain one of the character's labels (name/surname/first-name/alias) are examined; context extends +1 sentence forward and -1 backward only if that neighbor names NO character (345-352).
components.scope: Per scene (chapter). Base unit = sentence containing the character's name, extended ±1 no-name sentence; Guard-1 suppression window is asymmetric -10/+3 sentences (358-360); Guard 3 consults the FULL scene text (333-334).
components.invokedFrom: StoryValidationPipeline (pipeline.ts:42; critical errors short-circuit at 62-66); worker buildPronounStabilityValidator (agent9-run.ts:2072); pipeline drops its errors when policy validationEnabled=false (pipeline.ts:80-83).
components.knownLimitations: Three stacked suppression guards give it near-zero recall in mixed-gender chapters: Guard 1 (361-364) suppresses if ANY character of the wrong pronoun's gender is named within -10/+3 sentences — so Hugo-as-she is silenced whenever Beatrice or any female is named within 10 sentences back (reviewer examples 1-3 mostly MISSED). Guard 2 (369-377) suppresses if the character's own correct pronoun appears in the SAME sentence — mixed 'he...her' drift sentences pass. Guard 3 (385-389) suppresses extension-only pronouns when ANY character of that gender exists anywhere in the scene. Reviewer example 4 ('she felt the ache of her own failure', viewpoint Hugo, no name in sentence): the sentence enters analysis only as an extension of an adjacent Hugo-naming sentence; then it is extension-only, so Guard 3 kills it if any female is named anywhere in ch10 — and if no adjacent sentence names Hugo at all (deep viewpoint narration), the sentence is never examined. MISSED structurally: there is no viewpoint/POV concept.

components.name: ProseConsistencyValidator.checkPronounDrift proximity-window heuristic (pronoun_drift, severity moderate)
components.lines: checkPronounDrift 504-626 (window heuristic 535-623); stripDialogueFromWindow 42-46; findNamePositions 628-636; genderToPronouns 52-61; oppositePronouns 64-73
components.what: Pattern classes: any wrong-gender subject|object|possessive within a character-name window (regex at 586). NO reflexives, NO 'hers'. Association: pure proximity — a wrong pronoun anywhere within ±200 chars of a mention of the character's first name or surname (windowSize 552) is attributed to that character. Dialogue is stripped from the window (curly + straight double quotes, ≤300 chars) before testing. One error max per character per scene, seeded by the high-precision detectors' flaggedPairs (515, 565-567).
components.scope: ±200-character window around each first-name/surname mention, per scene; competitor suppression searches the mention's full PARAGRAPH plus the window (A_62 Item 13 widening, 595-605).
components.invokedFrom: ProseConsistencyValidator.validate (334) → StoryValidationPipeline (pipeline.ts:44); errors filtered out under relaxed/off policy (pipeline.ts:80-83); message prefix 'Pronoun drift for "<name>"' is the parsing contract for the worker's extractPronounTargetNames (agent9-run.ts:1599).
components.knownLimitations: Competitor guard (603-608): ANY opposite-gender cast name-part (≥3 chars) in the paragraph-or-window suppresses — so Hugo-as-she is silent wherever any female character is named in the same paragraph (examples 1-3 largely missed in ensemble scenes). Requires the drifted character's NAME within 200 chars: reviewer example 4 in nameless viewpoint-narration paragraphs is invisible; it fires only if 'Hugo'/'Vane' happens to sit within 200 chars of the 'she' AND no female name is in the paragraph. Cannot say WHICH pronoun or WHERE (message only says 'a female pronoun nearby'). Because it keys on the wrong pronoun being near the RIGHT name, self-consistent whole-paragraph drift with no names has no anchor and is missed.

components.name: detectAttributionFlips — high-precision dialogue-tag flip detector (pronoun_drift kind 'attribution_flip')
components.lines: 180-240; SPEECH_VERBS 99-103; buildGenderedTokenIndex 130-150; narrationOnly 158-165; wired into checkPronounDrift at 516-533
components.what: Pattern class: ONLY narration dialogue-tag subject pronouns ('"...," he said') — closing-quote + he|she + past-tense speech verb (tagPattern 185), with straight-quote parity check (190-193) so in-dialogue pronouns are excluded. Association: nearest-preceding-gendered-referent — scans back through narration-only text (dialogue stripped) for cast-name tokens AND bare subject pronouns; the nearest one wins (208-226). Flags only when the nearest referent is opposite-gender, no same-gender cast name exists in the window, and the nearest opposite referent is a NAME (228-231).
components.scope: Scan-back window = current paragraph plus at most ONE paragraph boundary back (198-203).
components.invokedFrom: detectPronounDriftEvents (323-325) → ProseConsistencyValidator.checkPronounDrift (517); duplicated as detectAttributionFlipsLocal in packages/rubric-score/src/facts.ts:342 (rubric pronounsUnstable extractor, facts.ts:207-225, hard-cap at hard-caps.ts:53).
components.knownLimitations: Catches ONLY speech-tag flips — reviewer example 4 (pure narration) can never match. Self-consistent drift defeats it: because bare pronouns count as referents (221-226), a paragraph already drifted to 'she' for Hugo makes the nearest referent female, so 'she said' AGREES and no flag fires — i.e. it only catches the first tag after a correctly-gendered referent. sameGenderNamePresent guard (230) suppresses whenever any female cast name is in the 2-paragraph window (kills mixed scenes, examples 1-3). Deliberately precision-first per the 76-83 header comment: 'Precision over recall'.

components.name: detectImpossibleSelfReferences — high-precision self-reference detector (pronoun_drift kind 'impossible_self_reference')
components.what: Pattern classes: (a) wrong-gender REFLEXIVE after a cast-name sentence subject ('Eleanor composed himself', 287); (b) wrong-gender POSSESSIVE over a closed list of personal-object nouns ('Eleanor ... adjusted his gloves', 288 — body parts/attire/effects only). Association: the sentence must BEGIN with 1-3 capitalized tokens that resolve to a gendered cast-name token (260-278); everything after the subject is scanned. Suppressions: intervening opposite-gender pronoun before the hit (284, 294), unnamed person-role noun before the hit (A_62 Item 13 FP2, 302), any wrong-gender cast token anywhere in the paragraph (304-309).
components.scope: Sentence, within a paragraph loop; dialogue stripped per paragraph (263-266).
components.invokedFrom: detectPronounDriftEvents (323-325) → ProseConsistencyValidator.checkPronounDrift (517); local copy in rubric-score facts.ts (~line 400s, combined at 465).
components.knownLimitations: Never catches wrong SUBJECT pronouns ('she felt') — only reflexives and possessive+SELF_NOUN. Reviewer example 4 fails twice: the sentence subject is 'She', not a cast name, so subjectPattern resolves no gendered subject and the sentence is skipped; and even rewritten as 'Hugo felt the ache of her own failure', 'failure' is not in SELF_NOUNS (abstract nouns absent — list is gloves/hat/composure/gaze etc.), so no hit. Requires the drifted character to be NAMED as sentence-opener — viewpoint narration paragraphs with zero names are invisible. Paragraph-level wrong-gender cast-mention suppression (304-309) silences mixed scenes.

components.name: repairPronouns — sentence-level repair pass (detection-by-repair: single-mention + inheritance + guards)
components.lines: repairPronouns 384-598 (EXPORTED); repairPronounsInSegment 191-235; classifySingleMentionSkip 325-351 (Guards B/D/E); scanDialogue 360-382; leadingGenderedAppositive 83-90; Guard C 496-516; T2-7 actor/object split 543-582; buildCharacterInfo 122-157; characterMentionedIn 163-173
components.what: Pattern classes: all four forms — subject, object, possessive, reflexive — via wrong-pronoun regex replace (198-235), with a her-object-vs-possessive heuristic (next-token lookahead, 213-230). Association rules, in order per sentence: (1) exactly ONE character named → all wrong pronouns are theirs, unless Guard B (leading subject pronoun + directional verb at the named OBJECT, e.g. 'He turned to Lady Beatrice' → clear anchor, 333-337/459-464), Guard D (named char is PERCEIVER — pronouns after perception verb belong to the object, 340-341), Guard E (correct+wrong genders both present → wrong ones belong elsewhere, 344-348); (2) ZERO named → inherit lastSingleCharacter (last-named-single antecedent), gated by Guard C: ≥2 opposite-gender pronouns AND (anchor was cross-paragraph-inherited OR someone of that gender was named in the paragraph) → protect the self-consistent run (511-516, A_62 Item 13 TP3 relaxation); gendered-title appositive 'the mistress, he' overrides Guard C (481-494); (3) 2+ named same gender → repair against first (527-541); mixed genders → skip except T2-7 last-named-is-object split in onlyNames mode (550-582). Dialogue segments never repaired and never move the anchor (443-455).
components.scope: Sentence within paragraph; anchor resets at paragraph boundary unless crossParagraphInheritance, which carries it only when the new paragraph's OPENING sentence names zero characters (419-433).
components.invokedFrom: repairChapterPronouns (768); worker applyDeterministicPronounSweep (agent9-run.ts:2476, full-cast, monotonic-guarded 2486-2499); worker applyTargetedPronounSweep (agent9-run.ts:1635, onlyNames from validator errors); gated by getPronounPolicySettings().checkingEnabled (agent9-run.ts:3481).
components.knownLimitations: This is a REPAIR whose implied detection has the exact hole of reviewer example 4: a nameless viewpoint-narration paragraph gets its anchor only via cross-paragraph inheritance → anchorInherited=true → Guard C unconditionally protects any segment with ≥2 opposite pronouns — and 'she felt the ache of her own failure' has exactly 2 (she + her). So self-consistent viewpoint drift with no antecedent in window is protected BY DESIGN (the guard exists because run_1d55f7c7 flipped Margaret's correct run). If the previous paragraph's last-named single character is female (ensemble scenes), the drift even inherits a female anchor and reads as CORRECT. The TP3 relaxation (514) only rescues same-paragraph anchors, i.e. requires Hugo named earlier in the same paragraph with no female named there. Also: onlyNames targeting depends on the validators having flagged the character at all — the recall gaps above propagate.

components.name: repairDialogueAttributionPronouns — speaker-tag repair
components.what: Pattern class: closing-quote + optional comma + he|she|they + attribution verb (629). Association: scan back ≤800 chars bounded at the nearest paragraph break, locate the opening quote, collect characters named BEFORE it; repairs only when exactly ONE character is named and the tag pronoun contradicts their gender (641-668).
components.scope: Per paragraph (called per-paragraph by repairChapterPronouns 773-777), lookback window ≤800 chars / one paragraph.
components.knownLimitations: 0 or 2+ pre-quote named characters → skip (658). Tag verbs list (624-625) is shorter than the validator's SPEECH_VERBS — e.g. 'muttered', 'remarked', 'snapped' are detected by detectAttributionFlips but not repairable here. Only they/he/she tags; narration outside tags untouched. Irrelevant to reviewer example 4.

components.name: repairByMajorityVote — chapter-level majority sweep
components.what: For each gendered character named in the chapter, counts ALL male vs female pronouns in the FULL chapter text (712-719 — no character-proximity attribution whatsoever) and, if wrong-gender count ≤3 AND ≤30% of total (727-728), runs repairPronounsInSegment over the entire chapter for that character. Explicitly built to catch residual drift the sentence pass missed 'because Hale was last named and she appeared one sentence later' (693-695).
components.knownLimitations: STRUCTURALLY DEAD in any mixed-gender chapter: the counts are global chapter pronoun totals, not per-character attributions, so with Hugo AND Beatrice both active, female pronouns are legion (>3 and >30%) and the ≤3/≤30% gate never opens for either character — all four reviewer examples occur in a story with a mixed cast, so this pass contributes nothing. It only ever fires in near-single-gender chapters with ≤3 stray pronouns.

components.name: repairChapterPronouns — three-pass orchestrator + normalizeTitles
components.what: Pipeline per chapter: (1) normalizeTitles ('the doctor Finch' → 'Dr. Finch'), (2) repairPronouns over the joined full-chapter text with crossParagraphInheritance:true (768), (3) repairDialogueAttributionPronouns per paragraph (773-777), (4) repairByMajorityVote over the full chapter (789).
components.invokedFrom: Worker per-chapter post-processing applyDeterministicProsePostProcessing (agent9-run.ts:2746, monotonic-guarded via countChapterPronounMismatches 2756-2769, A_52 item 6) and inside applyTargetedPronounSweep (agent9-run.ts:1649).
components.knownLimitations: Union of the three passes' gaps: no pass models chapter viewpoint, so viewpoint-narration drift with no name in the inheritance chain (example 4) escapes all three. repairCount is a change-counter, not a defect report — detection telemetry is indirect.

components.name: Pronoun policy gating + pipeline error filter
components.lines: PronounPolicy type 250; Agent9ValidationConfig 238-242; defaults pronoun_policy 'strict' 795-797, pronoun_gate_parity_enabled true 733; getPronounPolicySettings 1690-1716 (EXPORTED); getPronounPolicy 1718-1720 (EXPORTED); derivePronounPolicyFromLegacyFlags 1678-1688; filter in pipeline.ts:80-83
components.what: strict = deterministic repair ON + validator errors ON; relaxed = repair ON, errors OFF; verify = repair OFF, errors ON (detection-only, errors flow to report/rubric); off = both OFF. StoryValidationPipeline strips pronoun_gender_mismatch and pronoun_drift from the final report when validationEnabled=false (pipeline.ts:80-83). Runtime-read (never frozen at module load, per MEMORY module-const trap).
components.knownLimitations: Under 'relaxed' the detectors still run but their findings are silently discarded from the report — a drift-heavy story can validate clean. The high-precision detectors (detectPronounDriftEvents) are the only ones whose signal also reaches the rubric independently (rubric-score facts.ts local copy), so under relaxed/off the rubric copy is the sole remaining pronoun detection.

components.name: Worker: countChapterPronounMismatches — monotonic-guard metric
components.what: Counts wrong-gender pronouns ONLY in sentences that name exactly one gender of known-gender character (full name/first/surname labels ≥3 chars, quoted speech stripped 2436). Used as before/after comparator so applyDeterministicPronounSweep (2489-2499) and the per-chapter repairChapterPronouns call (2756-2769) are reverted if they INCREASE mismatches (run_1d55f7c7 regression guard).
components.knownLimitations: Blind to the exact class it most needs to see: a sentence naming NO character contributes zero (2444), so viewpoint-narration drift (example 4) is invisible to the monotonicity check — a sweep that fixed or worsened such sentences moves the metric not at all. Mixed-gender sentences skipped (2446).

components.name: Worker: buildPronounStabilityValidator (A_57 D5) + applyPronounGuardedMutation
components.what: Wraps CharacterConsistencyValidator (with RC2.2 genderOverride) into a score = 100 − 10×(pronoun_gender_mismatch count); mutateThenValidate reverts any deterministic post-processing pass (grounding-lead, alias substitution, etc.) that raises the count. Count-free violation label (A_58 fix, 2080-2084) so partial repairs are not reverted. Measurement failure → score 100 (gate inert, 2074-2076).
components.scope: Full prose, all chapters, on each guarded mutation.
components.knownLimitations: Inherits CharacterConsistencyValidator's recall wholesale: mismatches that validator cannot see (all four reviewer examples in mixed scenes; all viewpoint narration) are outside the guarded metric, so post-LLM passes can still corrupt or fail to protect those regions (consistent with the MEMORY note that post-processing runs after validation).

components.name: Worker: targeted repair chain — extractPronounTargetNames / applyTargetedPronounSweep / rescue + parity passes
components.lines: extractPronounTargetNames 1582-1609; applyTargetedPronounSweep 1611-1680; deterministic rescue 5683-5721; targeted rescue 5723-5738; ANALYSIS_43 Phase 1b parity pass 5793-5817 (flag default true, generation-params.ts:733); residual gate warning 5819-5829; cycle re-targeting 6011
components.what: Parses validator error MESSAGES with two regexes — 'Pronoun drift for "<name>"' and 'Character "<name>" has incorrect pronouns' (1599-1600) — to build the onlyNames set, then runs repairPronouns(onlyNames, crossParagraphInheritance) plus full repairChapterPronouns on chapters mentioning a target. The parity pass re-runs after victim/alias mutations and is intentionally independent of pronoun_policy (5797-5801, run 6aea3501 fix).

components.knownLimitations: Detection-bounded: repairs are only attempted for characters the two validators actually FLAGGED — every suppression gap upstream (mixed-scene guards, viewpoint narration) means no target, hence no repair; probe #1 shipped with severe drift precisely because nothing flagged Hugo/Beatrice/Hale in those chapters. Message-regex coupling is fragile: any wording change in either validator silently zeroes the target set.

keyFindings: EXPORT INDEX (every exported pronoun function): packages/story-validation/src/pronoun-repair.ts — repairPronouns:384, repairChapterPronouns:752, normalizeTitles:817 (types CastEntry:17, PronounRepairResult:237, PronounRepairOptions:257); prose-consistency-validator.ts — detectAttributionFlips:180, detectImpossibleSelfReferences:253, detectPronounDriftEvents:323, class ProseConsistencyValidator:327 (types PronounDriftCastEntry:85, PronounDriftEvent:90); character-validator.ts — class CharacterConsistencyValidator:73, buildAllowedNameParts:36, anonymiseNamedWalkOns:51; generation-params.ts — getPronounPolicySettings:1690, getPronounPolicy:1718 (type PronounPolicy:250); re-exports index.ts:11 (prose-consistency *), :40 (repair fns), :46 (CharacterConsistencyValidator); apps/worker/src/jobs/agents/agent9-run.ts — buildPronounStabilityValidator:2058, applyDeterministicPronounSweep:2457 (internal: extractPronounTargetNames:1582, applyTargetedPronounSweep:1611, countChapterPronounMismatches:2421).

VERDICT ON THE FOUR REVIEWER EXAMPLES: (1) Hugo-as-she, (2) Beatrice-as-he, (3) Hale-feminine are each detectable in principle by BOTH validators, but every detector carries an opposite-gender-nearby suppression guard (character-validator.ts:361-364 wider -10/+3 window; prose-consistency-validator.ts:603-608 paragraph+window competitor guard; :230 sameGenderNamePresent; :304-309 paragraph cast-mention) — in an ensemble mystery where Hugo, Beatrice and Hale share chapters, these guards suppress nearly every instance, which is exactly why probe #1 shipped with severe drift undetected. (4) 'she felt the ache of her own failure' (viewpoint narration, no female name near) is missed by EVERY layer for independent structural reasons — no detector or repair models a chapter viewpoint/POV character.

Why example 4 escapes each layer: character-validator.ts:337 requires the character's NAME in the sentence (viewpoint narration has none; as an extension sentence it is killed by Guard 3 :385-389 if any female exists in the scene). prose-consistency-validator.ts:552 requires the name within ±200 chars. detectAttributionFlips only sees speech tags (:185). detectImpossibleSelfReferences :260-278 requires a cast-name sentence SUBJECT ('She' resolves to nothing) and never checks subject pronouns; even 'her own failure' fails because 'failure' is not in SELF_NOUNS :107-111. repairPronouns' inheritance path is explicitly blocked: the sentence carries 2 female pronouns, and with a cross-paragraph-inherited anchor Guard C (pronoun-repair.ts:511-516) unconditionally protects self-consistent opposite-gender runs (anchorInherited=true bypasses the A_62 TP3 relaxation). repairByMajorityVote :727-728 can never fire in a mixed-gender chapter because it counts chapter-global pronoun totals, not per-character attributions. countChapterPronounMismatches (agent9-run.ts:2444) scores only name-bearing sentences, so even the monotonic guard metric is blind to this class.

ANTECEDENT MODEL IS UNIFORMLY NAME-PROXIMITY, NEVER DISCOURSE STATE: association mechanisms are (a) name-in-sentence with ±1-sentence extension (character-validator), (b) ±200-char window around a name (prose-consistency), (c) nearest preceding gendered referent within ≤2 paragraphs where bare pronouns themselves count as referents (detectAttributionFlips :221-226 — meaning an already-drifted run self-certifies), (d) last-named-single-character inheritance with paragraph reset (repairPronouns). None maintains a per-chapter viewpoint character, so ROLE-pronoun contamination that produces long self-consistent wrong-gender runs in narrator-proximate prose (the reviewer's diagnosis) has no antecedent in any window and is invisible end-to-end.

COVERAGE HOLES BY PRONOUN FORM: reflexives himself/herself are repaired (pronoun-repair.ts:109-110) and detected only via detectImpossibleSelfReferences' wrong-reflexive branch (:287); CharacterConsistencyValidator.findIncorrectPronouns checks he/she/him/her/his only (:391-405) — no himself/herself/hers; the prose-consistency window regex (:586) likewise omits reflexives and 'hers'. Possessive 'her' for a male character is detected only via the object-form check (character-validator.ts:400). CharacterConsistencyValidator does NOT strip dialogue; ProseConsistencyValidator and all repair passes do.

THE REPAIR CHAIN IS DETECTION-BOUNDED: agent9-run.ts's targeted rescue (5723-5738) and the pronoun_gate_parity pass (5793-5817) build their target set exclusively by regex-parsing the two validators' error messages (extractPronounTargetNames:1599-1600). Characters the guards suppressed are never targeted, and the broad full-cast sweep (applyDeterministicPronounSweep:2457) is itself reverted per-chapter if countChapterPronounMismatches rises — a metric blind to nameless sentences. Net effect: precision machinery is layered and mutually reinforcing, but recall for viewpoint-narration drift is structurally zero, matching the historical posture (ANALYSIS_20 rewrites caused 15-17 errors/run; every guard since — Guard C, monotonic revert, D5 — was added to prevent over-repair, each one trading away recall).

Policy note: default pronoun_policy is 'strict' (generation-params.ts:795); under 'relaxed' the pipeline silently drops both pronoun error types (pipeline.ts:80-83) while under 'verify' detection flows to the report but the deterministic fixer is off; the rubric-score copy of the two high-precision detectors (facts.ts:342,465) is the only pronoun signal independent of this gate.
